title: GitHub Actions
summary: How GitHub Actions workflows are stored, triggered, permitted and gated on GitHub, and which of those rules change what a coding agent can expect from a run.

sections.label: Where config lives
sections.text: Workflows are YAML files with a .yml or .yaml extension in the .github/workflows directory of the repository. A repository can have several workflows, such as one testing pull requests and one deploying on a release. The on key lists the events that start a workflow, and each job runs on a runner and executes steps.

sections.label: Conventional commands
sections.text: With the GitHub CLI, gh workflow run WORKFLOW starts a workflow that declares workflow_dispatch and gh run watch follows a run. gh run list shows recent runs and gh run view --job JOB_ID --log prints a job log. gh run rerun RUN_ID --failed reruns only the failed jobs of a run.

sections.label: How CI is declared
sections.text:
# Illustrative, the echo step is a placeholder.
name: ci
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - run: echo "placeholder"

sections.label: Where review conventions live
sections.text: GitHub reads CODEOWNERS from .github/, the root or docs/, in that order, taking the first file found. Pull requests use the file on the base branch, and the last matching pattern wins. A pull_request_template.md file can live in the root, docs/ or .github/, and templates work only once merged into the default branch. Branch protection can require code owner review and status checks before merging.

sections.label: Gotchas
items: schedule, workflow_dispatch, repository_dispatch, issue_comment and workflow_run only trigger a run if the workflow file exists on the default branch.

Events caused by GITHUB_TOKEN do not create new workflow runs, except workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch, and a pull request opened by a workflow with that token gets runs that wait for approval.
In pull requests from forks, secrets other than GITHUB_TOKEN are not passed to the runner and GITHUB_TOKEN is read only.

Setting any permissions key makes every unlisted permission none, and a new personal repository defaults to read access for contents and packages, with workflows unable to create or approve pull requests.
Required status checks must be successful, skipped or neutral before merging, and a job name reused across workflows can give ambiguous checks that block the merge.
Caches restore only from the current branch, the default branch or a pull request base branch, and unused caches are removed after 7 days.
A concurrency group runs one job or workflow at a time, queuing a new run cancels the pending one by default, and cancel-in-progress true also cancels the running one.

sections.label: What Atlas provides
sections.text: Selecting GitHub Actions adds the GitHub Actions pipelines profile with its review questions and checks. The profile does not read workflow files, run a workflow or verify branch protection.

sections.label: Check in your environment
sections.text: Confirm which workflow files exist on the default branch, which checks the target branch requires, the repository workflow permission setting, and whether gh is installed and authenticated.

basis: GitHub documentation on docs.github.com read on 2026-10-11, plus one illustrative workflow example.
confidence: Documented behavior has scoped sources that still need review. The YAML example and the Atlas profile text are illustrative and proposed.

catalog.applicability: Use when a repository is hosted on GitHub and its checks run as GitHub Actions workflows under .github/workflows.
catalog.limits: Catalogue inclusion does not verify your repository settings, installed CLI, runner availability or whether a workflow passes.
